editorial_thesis: Make automation earn trust at its boundaries: stop suspicious code before CI, pause browser agents for people, and measure model choices inside governed clients.

topic_groups.title: Supply-chain Defensive Defaults
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A clustered July 28 release set changes the default posture at publish, dependency, and CI execution time; it is a meaningful, fresh security-operating signal and a coverage gap since the July 23 runtime patch sweep.

sources.title: GitHub Actions holds potentially malicious workflows for approval
sources.why_selected: Stops a compromised credential from immediately turning a workflow change into CI-secret theft.
sources.usefulness: Enable least-privilege Actions tokens; review held runs through an incident playbook.

sources.title: npm publish-time malware scanning and dual-use metadata
sources.why_selected: Release pipelines that immediately install a just-published package now have a real availability dependency.
sources.usefulness: Make package smoke tests retry-aware; use trusted publishing for client packages.

sources.title: Dependabot alerts on malicious packages across more ecosystems
sources.why_selected: Detection coverage broadens beyond one registry and converts community malware intelligence into repository alerts.
sources.usefulness: Confirm Dependabot malware alerts at organization level; route alerts into the same triage queue as vulnerabilities.

topic_groups.title: Human Checkpoints for Browser Agents
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Browser agents are moving from brittle manual intervention to explicit pause-and-resume contracts, a practical control gap distinct from yesterday’s protocol and memory coverage.

sources.title: Browser Run adds structured handoff for Human in the Loop
sources.why_selected: Login walls and unexpected prompts become named workflow states rather than silent browser-run failures.
sources.usefulness: Use for supervised intake, vendor portals, and authenticated client research where credentials never enter the agent prompt.

sources.title: Cloudflare MCP servers support the MCP 2026-07-28 Specification
sources.why_selected: Explicit state and transport reduce hidden continuity assumptions around agent tool sessions.
sources.usefulness: Use /mcp for new connections and test reconnect behavior in client tool chains.

sources.title: Introducing Loops
sources.why_selected: It is a useful operating reference: recurring agent work needs visible instructions, configuration, and traceable outcomes.
sources.usefulness: Apply the pattern to weekly client-status drafts or issue triage—review before dispatching code work.

topic_groups.title: Governed Model Choice + Adoption Evidence
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The Copilot surface now couples a new selectable reasoning model with client-specific policy and richer attribution, creating an actionable model-evaluation loop rather than another model announcement.

sources.title: Grok 4.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
sources.why_selected: A candidate model is available inside existing PR, audit, and policy controls—useful for a bounded comparison, not blanket rollout.
sources.usefulness: Run a fixed set of exploration and terminal tasks; compare completed work, review burden, latency, and spend.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot app usage metrics now expand across report rollups
sources.why_selected: It closes an attribution gap: model experiments can be evaluated by workflow surface rather than license count alone.
sources.usefulness: Track an opt-in pilot against a baseline and pair the API with PR-quality review.

sources.title: Manage GitHub Copilot app access with a dedicated policy
sources.why_selected: Separate client policy enables a smaller experiment surface while retaining central plugin and audit controls.
sources.usefulness: Enable only the client needed for the pilot; keep review, checks, and audit history mandatory.
